analysis:
All four units are documentation-only changes: docs/reference/configuration.md, which has a date bump and a rewritten `backend.enabled_models` row, plus the visible text of the cluster link and console sections, and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md, which has a date bump and additions on `load_model`, `prefetch_model` and `desired_models`. No executable code changed, so no security control was weakened by this diff.

The new documented behavior is an operator model filter. Without Autopilot, a coordinator `load_model` or `prefetch_model` for a model outside the filter is refused with `model_not_selected`. `desired_models` alias successors outside the filter are not fetched, staged, served or used to drop the previous build. This tightens the trust boundary between the coordinator and the provider (TB-002, TB-003) and is consistent with the adversarial-coordinator-messages posture. It also limits unintended downloads and disk use (T-016). The docs say that with Autopilot enabled, only its lease and set gates can admit such a build. That is a documented design and not evidence of a bypass.

The unchanged cluster link text in configuration.md describes root-privileged commands run through osascript. It says the interface name is validated, `--device` is never placed in a command, and the keeper is built key by key from fixed values. I found no new claim there that contradicts the threat model.

The enforcement lives in `provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+ModelSelection.swift` (`operatorFilterAllows`, `autopilotAllowsModel`), which is not supplied. Whether it matches the documentation is unverified, and the next review pass should check the filter semantics there. In particular:
- `[]` filters nothing.
- A hand edit applies only at the next start.
- A live `switch` replaces the filter immediately.
- The filter should not be bypassed by coordinator commands when Autopilot is not consented.

The patch excerpt for configuration.md is truncated, so I could not see the full diff of that file.
